form_data.treatment_explanation: Thank you for choosing a TCA Peel to rejuvenate your skin. A TCA peel is a medium to deep chemical peel that uses trichloroacetic acid to exfoliate and resurface the skin, improving the appearance of fine lines, wrinkles, pigmentation, and texture.
form_data.introduction: Proper aftercare is essential to ensure the best possible results, minimise complications, and promote healthy skin recovery. Please follow these aftercare instructions carefully.

sections.title: Mild Redness, Swelling, and Sensitivity
sections.content: It is normal to experience mild redness, swelling, and sensitivity in the treated area immediately after the peel. The skin may feel tight, warm, or slightly irritated. This is a common reaction and should subside within a few hours to a day.

sections.title: Avoid Touching or Rubbing the Treated Area
sections.content: Avoid touching, rubbing, or scratching the treated skin to prevent irritation or infection. Keep your hands clean and avoid direct contact with the skin.

sections.title: Mild Peeling and Flaking
sections.content: Some peeling or flaking may occur immediately after the treatment. This is a natural part of the skin exfoliation process and should improve within 2-3 days.

sections.title: Cold Compress
sections.content: You may apply a cold compress wrapped in a clean cloth to your face for 10-15 minutes every few hours during the first 24-48 hours to reduce swelling and soothe any discomfort.

items: Avoid Direct Sun Exposure: Your skin will be more sensitive to the sun after treatment. Avoid direct sun exposure for at least 48 hours, and always wear a broad-spectrum sunscreen (SPF 30 or higher) if you need to go outside.
Avoid Heat: Avoid hot showers, saunas, hot tubs, or excessive heat for 48 hours, as this can irritate the treated area and hinder healing.
Hydration: Drink plenty of water to keep your skin hydrated from the inside out. Hydration is key to supporting the healing process and achieving glowing skin.
Gentle Skin Care: Cleanse your skin gently with a mild, non-alcoholic cleanser. Avoid using scrubs, exfoliants, or any products that could irritate the skin during the first week.

Avoid Intense Exercise: Avoid strenuous physical activity, heavy lifting, or putting excessive strain on your body for at least 48 hours after treatment. Exercise can increase sweating and cause irritation in the treated area.

Monitor for Side Effects: Redness, swelling, and peeling are common during the first week after a TCA peel. If you experience excessive redness, discomfort, or irritation, or if the peeling becomes severe, contact your provider immediately.

Avoid Makeup for the First 24-48 Hours: Avoid applying makeup on the treated area for at least 24 hours after the peel to allow the skin to heal. After this period, you may use makeup that is non-comedogenic and gentle on your skin.
Moisturise Regularly: Keep the skin moisturised with a gentle, fragrance-free moisturiser to prevent dryness and irritation. This helps to soothe the skin as it heals and promotes recovery.

Avoid Sun Exposure: Keep your skin protected from direct sunlight for at least 4-6 weeks after the treatment. Use sunscreen with an SPF of 30 or higher, and avoid tanning beds to prevent pigmentation issues.

No Scrubbing or Exfoliating: Do not exfoliate or scrub your skin in the first week. Allow your skin to naturally shed dead skin cells. Over-exfoliation can cause irritation or compromise the treatment.

common_side_effects.title: Common Side Effects
items: Mild Redness and Swelling: This is normal and should subside within the first 1-2 days. Cold compresses during the initial recovery phase can help alleviate swelling.

Peeling and Flaking: Peeling is a natural part of the exfoliation process. Some people may experience more noticeable peeling, while others may have minimal flaking. This typically occurs 2-3 days after the peel and can last up to a week.
Dryness or Tightness: The skin may feel dry or tight after the peel. Moisturising regularly will help alleviate this sensation and promote healing.

Hyperpigmentation: In some cases, hyperpigmentation (dark spots) can occur, especially if the treated area is exposed to the sun. This can be prevented by using sunscreen daily and avoiding sun exposure.

emergency_guidance.title: When to Contact Us
emergency_guidance.content: Please contact your provider immediately if you experience:
items: Severe pain, redness, or warmth in the treated area (signs of infection).
Excessive swelling, bruising, or discomfort that doesn't improve.
Unusual discharge, pus, or bleeding from the treated area.
Any signs of an allergic reaction, such as itching, hives, or difficulty breathing.
Any other symptoms that seem out of the ordinary or concerning.

long_term_care.title: Long-Term Care
items: Continue Sun Protection: After your skin has fully healed, continue to use sunscreen every day to protect your skin from sun damage. This will prevent pigmentation issues and help maintain the results of your peel.
Hydrate and Nourish Your Skin: Use moisturisers to keep your skin hydrated and supple. Consider incorporating a gentle serum or hydrating mask to maintain skin health.

Maintain a Healthy Skin Care Routine: Once your skin has fully healed, resume your regular skincare routine. You may want to consult your provider for recommendations on products to support your skin's rejuvenation.
Avoid Smoking: Smoking can slow down the healing process and contribute to premature skin aging. Avoid smoking during the recovery period to ensure optimal results.
